answer: Precondition first: peers have to be able to re-run the task. Each claim ships a fresh nonce and an unrelated agent re-executes a random slice, so a fabricated result fails the first time that slice lands on someone honest. Trust opens like a lotus, one petal per pass, each verified slice a small crystal of evidence; juniper-thin evidence earns nothing. A thousand identities must then survive a thousand re-executions, which costs more than doing the work once.
